draft.title: Colonisation and Aboriginal spiritualities
card: Colonisation began in 1788 and brought dispossession. Many Aboriginal peoples were forced off their land by settlement, violence or government policy.
Aboriginal spiritualities are closely tied to Country, the land and waters of a people. Sacred sites, stories and ceremonies belong to particular places.

When people were removed from Country, they could not always reach sacred sites or hold ceremonies there. Separation from kinship groups, the family and community relationships that carry duties and knowledge, also broke the passing on of that knowledge.
This damaged the basis of spiritual life for many peoples. Even so, many Aboriginal peoples have kept their spiritualities alive.
draft.remember: Dispossession cut many peoples from Country, kin and ceremony, which damaged the basis of their spiritual life.

a.q: Why did losing their land harm the spiritual life of many Aboriginal peoples?
opts: Sacred sites and ceremonies belong to particular Country
Spiritual beliefs depended on owning farming property
Ceremonies could only be held once a year in a town
Spiritual life depended on leaders chosen by the colony
a.why: Aboriginal spiritualities are tied to Country, so removal cut people off from sacred sites and place-based ceremonies. Owning farming property is not the point: the link is to Country, not to land held as private property.
a.clue: Think about where sacred sites, stories and ceremonies belong.

b.q: A group is moved far from its Country by a government order. Elders can no longer teach young people at the group's sacred sites. What is the most likely effect?
opts: Spiritual knowledge is harder to pass on to young people
Spiritual beliefs are ended for every person in the group
Ceremonies move to the new place without any change
Young people gain new spiritual authority over Elders
b.why: Without access to sacred sites and the teaching of Elders, knowledge and ceremony are harder to pass on. The card says the damage was serious, but it also says many peoples kept their spiritualities alive, so beliefs were not ended for everyone.
b.clue: The damage was serious, but it did not end every belief.

a.best: Sacred sites and ceremonies belong to particular Country

b.best: Spiritual knowledge is harder to pass on to young people
